title: Phoenix Protocol: Verify VPC visibility using describe-vpcs (read-only, deterministic).
objectives: Understand the concept of VPC visibility in AWS
Learn how to use the `describe-vpcs` command to view available VPCs
Demonstrate ability to identify visible VPCs

mission_brief.situation: You are operating as a secure cloud operator in an authorized sandbox where resources may or may not exist.
mission_brief.mission: Verify access safely using read-only AWS CLI commands without assuming any pre-existing resources.
mission_brief.execution: Run discovery-only commands and validate success by deterministic behavior (successful execution), not resource presence.

content.concept: VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is a virtual network dedicated to a customer's AWS account. Visibility refers to the accessibility of this VPC to other AWS services and accounts. Deterministic validation means you confirm the command executed successfully without relying on resource names
content.walkthrough: To view available VPCs, navigate to the AWS Management Console and search for 'describe-vpcs' in the CLI or terminal. Alternatively, use the AWS CLI command `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --output json` in your local environment.
checkpoints: Run the `describe-vpcs` command without any arguments
Verify the output contains at least one VPC ID
Check if VPC visibility is set to 'enabled' for a specific VPC
common_mistakes: Assuming all VPCs are visible by default
Not specifying the `--output json` flag when running CLI commands
Using an outdated AWS CLI version that does not support the `describe-vpcs` command

lab.setup: Ensure AWS CLI is configured with sandbox credentials. Do not create, modify, or delete any resources.
safety: This lab is read-only and will not modify any resources in your AWS account
The CLI commands used are deterministic and will produce the same output regardless of your environment
No sensitive information, such as access keys or secret keys, will be required for this lab

elite_competence.role_simulation: Demonstrate expertise in AWS VPC visibility by identifying and explaining at least two visible VPCs.

bug_injection.bug: Operator assumes resources must exist and mislabels empty output as failure.
bug_injection.symptom: Student reports 'nothing returned' and believes permissions are broken.
bug_injection.fix: Explain empty-sandbox behavior and validate by successful execution + no errors, not by finding assets.

pass_conditions: The `describe-vpcs` command is run correctly with no errors
At least one VPC ID is present in the output
VPC visibility is set to 'enabled' for a specific VPC
fail_conditions: The `describe-vpcs` command fails due to incorrect permissions
No VPCs are visible despite having an enabled visibility setting

interrogation_questions: What is the purpose of VPC visibility in AWS?
How do you run the `describe-vpcs` command using the AWS CLI?
What might cause a VPC to be invisible to other AWS services?

legal_context.allowed: Executing read-only AWS CLI commands in an authorized sandbox or training account.
legal_context.prohibited: Creating, deleting, or modifying AWS resources without explicit authorization.

resume_bullets: Demonstrated understanding of VPC visibility in AWS
Successfully ran the `describe-vpcs` command using the AWS CLI
Identified and explained at least two visible VPCs
